items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: And for instance, Muggsy Spanier he loved Louis and you could hear Louis through all his playing.

ctx.x: Because things like that tend to evolve.

I was one of them. Benny Goodman's another and Muggsy Spanier and Frank Ieschemachler (Deschman??) and Bud Freeman. These guys were all stylists on their instruments and we had our influences. And for instance, Muggsy Spanier he loved Louis and you could hear Louis through all his playing. Although he wasn't copying any of Louis' licks. It's the same thing with me and Bix, when Bix said to me I like you kid, you sound like me but you don't copy me. It's the same thing with Louis. I mean, like Muggsy Spanier
he sounded like Louis but he didn't copy him. He played his own way but he did have, his influence was there. And what greater influence could a person have? In my opinion. Musically.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: Oh, I knew Tesh in 1925. When I went to Jimmy McPartland and Bud Freeman.

ctx.x: I didn't know that. I didn't know that. He had a big, heavy-shaped guy. I didn't know that. He played a long bass. I played with him in 1921. 1921 on the boat. I didn't know that. I didn't know that. He had Penico with him. He had Penico with him. He actually had Penico break his armband. 23, Penico had his armband out there. When you first did you know that? He played with him. He played with him in 1921. He played with him in 1921. He played with him in 1921. When did you first hear Tesh, Mark?

Oh, I knew Tesh in 1925. When I went to Jimmy McPartland and Bud Freeman. So when I left White City, grew up in Midway Gardens, I got a hold of Tesh and Jess. We really had a swinging band at that Midway. I was considered the best band in Chicago at that time. Midway. Is that so? Oh, yeah. We used to outdraw the Trianon. You know, the big name band. Oh, really? Oh, yeah. Whose band was that? It was just a house band. House band. Right. Was Midway out on the Midway? Out near there? That was in the 60th and the…

You know the further thing? I know the Muslim, but I didn't see the Muslim. Who was with Ted Lewis? When there ain't a town, I'm going out of that town. Or when you were playing the Palace there, I was at the Rose, and I didn't never get a chance to see you. You were playing the Palace right across the street.
